content:
ajay: Heads-up — started seeing a wave of spot evictions in us-west2 around 09:03 UTC, looks like interruption rate spiked to ~28% for the gpu-v100 pool. Impact: brief 503s, queue spikes, a few canary errors.

maria: Oof. Any patterns? specific sizes/models?

ajay: Mostly long-context batches (seq>2k) on gptq-large variants. Evictions correlate with sustained high batch occupancy.

cheng: Are we still scheduling standard tier into us-west2 spot by default? I thought we had soft-eviction turned on.

ajay: We do, but policy thresholds are conservative (eviction_rate>0.4 before failing over). This event stayed under that threshold but still noisy.

sophie: Suggestion: lower circuit-breaker threshold for pools with high tail latency impact. Proposed rule: if p90_eviction_rate > 0.15 for 2m OR p99_latency increases 25% -> trigger spill to fallback pools and model-variant fallback.

samir: +1. Also add an exponential backoff to return traffic to the spot pool (avoid oscillation). Example: cooldown windows 10m/30m/2h.

ajay: I sketched a quick config for testing, copyable:

```
fallback_policy:
  pool_level:
    circuit_breaker:
      eviction_rate_threshold: 0.15 # p90
      window: 120s
      cooldowns: [600s, 1800s, 7200s]
    spill_to: [dedicated-pool, cross-region-spot]
  model_fallback_order: [gptq-medium, gptq-small, cpu-int8]
  tier_routing:
    enterprise: prefer_dedicated
    standard: prefer_mixed
    free: prefer_spot
```

maria: Love the cooldowns. For model_fallback_order: can we annotate cost and expected latency delta so cost dashboards pick it up?

cheng: We should also consider region failover priority: us-west1 -> us-central1 -> eu-west1, but only if data residency permits. Add customer-level override.

sophie: Operational constraints: network egress spike when failing across regions. Need a pre-check that the target region has ephemeral network cap. If not, fallback to model variant fallback instead of cross-region spill.

ajay: Good point. Add a pre-flight check: `if region.network_utilization < 70% and region.available_gpus > 10` then allow cross-region spill.

infra-bot: Alert: spot_eviction_rate(us-west2,gpu-v100)=0.28 at 1795324835 UTC.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2027-0322-41 (auto-assign to eng-oncall), priority=P2.

samir: For rollout: canary on 5% of traffic (low-cost customers) for 30m, compare p99 latency & error rate. If pass, escalate to 25% then 100%. Keep cost delta metric.

maria: Metrics to watch: p99 latency, request_error_rate, prefix_cache_hit, token_cost_per_request. Also track model-fallback-rate and cross-region-egress_GB.

cheng: One more: ensure we surface user-visible reason codes for degraded responses (e.g., "fallback: model_variant:gptq-small" or "fallback: region:us-central1"). That helps SRE+support triage.

ajay: Agreed. We'll add a `fallback_reason` field on the response envelope and log in tracing.

sophie: Can infra team add a short-term mitigation? My vote: lower circuit-breaker threshold to 0.12 for this pool and enable a single-step model fallback (gptq-medium) for standard tier immediately. Rollback after 2h if no more evictions.

ajay: I'm going to push a canary patch to the control-plane config with those toggles now.

infra-bot: Deploy started: config/eviction-circuit-2027-03-22 canary -> 5% traffic.

maria: Monitoring dash updated -> new panel for pool_eviction_buckets + fallback_rate.

samir: If rollout looks good at 30m, I want a follow-up runbook entry: how to manually force per-customer routing (dedicated override) for incidents.

ajay: Will write the runbook snippet and post in #incidents.

cheng: Quick ask: can we add an automated tagging of sessions that experience fallback so Optimize team can tune quant profiles? Tagging = `fallback_tag:[region|model|pool]`.

ajay: Done. We'll include that in the canary.

sophie: Thanks all. Keep updates brief in thread. If it widens we escalate to incident channel. :thumbsup:
